source: src/components/community/PeerOrgDirectoryTable.tsx's own header comment ('spec 05 §5 component 3: peer-org directory, aggregate, pseudonymous') and CONFIRMED ABSENCE from the design source: `grep -i 'directory'` and `grep -i 'peer.org'` against README.md return nothing, and p12 (#p12, the Community artboard, docs/design/handoff-2026-09-06/'Caros Ledge UI System.dc.html') contains no directory/table markup — its content is the room/thread surface, not this aggregate table.
notes: This part is NOT one of the 17 UI-system artboards. Per CLAUDE.md rule 2 ('never fabricate') this spec does not invent a per-pixel design value to compare against — there is no design source stating one. What it checks instead: the general sitewide rules every part must follow regardless of artboard coverage (no literal UNSCORED anywhere; the component's own legacy `--color-*` tokens resolve to the SAME canonical values theme.css defines, so the legacy naming is migration debt, not a visual defect) — confirmed live, not asserted from reading theme.css alone.

Token resolution confirmed (theme.css): --color-bg-surface: var(--card) [#FFFFFF]; --color-border: var(--line-1) [rgba(0,0,0,.12)]; --color-text-muted: var(--ink-3) [#7A6E6C]; --color-text-primary: var(--ink) [#1A1A1A]. PeerOrgDirectoryTable.tsx reads the legacy names exclusively (never the canonical ones directly), which is exactly the migration-scaffolding pattern theme.css's own header describes ('legacy names are migration scaffolding for components later lanes still have to touch') — logged here, not fixed (this lane writes no product code).
